basis: Immunodeficiency and autoimmunity define immune forms; endocrine, ocular and skeletal abnormalities vary across the SHORT and immunodeficiency subgroups.
IgG4-mediated orbital/lacrimal inflammation; salivary and pancreatic inflammation each annotated 30-79%; nerve enlargement without common functional neuropathy is insufficient.
Central hypomyelination and peripheral demyelinating neuropathy define the disorder; optic atrophy occurs in only 5-29%.
Congenital absence or loss of a limb or limb segment is a structural musculoskeletal defect.
Direct pancreatic/salivary, biliary and orbital inflammatory lesions are each annotated 30-79%; Hashimoto thyroiditis is a separately diagnosed association.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal/neonatal platelets; intracranial hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Malignancy originates in the hard palate, part of the oral cavity.
Skeletal muscular dystrophy; cognitive impairment and learning disability occur in 30-79%; cardiomyopathy is 5-29%, with bundle branch block reported in one patient.
Skeletal dysplasia; callosal hypoplasia and retinal abnormalities each reported in 1/1 patient support brain/eye involvement; respiratory distress alone does not establish lung damage.
Locally infiltrating sweat duct-type adnexal neoplasm of nipple dermis/subcutis supports a cutaneous origin.
Chronic autoimmune cutaneous inflammation; systemic lupus involvement is not inherent to this cutaneous umbrella.
Cyst originates from tooth-development tissues; teeth and odontogenic structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Sterile neutrophilic skin ulceration; supplied myositis frequency of 80-99% supports muscle damage; RA, IBD and marrow disorders are separate associations.
Autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorders defined by intellectual disability; other organ defects vary by subtype.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy; contractures 3/3, corneal scarring 2/3 and bilateral vocal cord paresis 1/3 support joint, eye and upper-airway functional damage.
Dermal elastic-fiber disorder; aortic/valvular disease and joint/spinal abnormalities each occur in 30-79%; emphysema and bladder diverticula are only 5-29%.
Secondary open-angle glaucoma damages the eye; elevated local episcleral venous pressure does not establish a separate cardiovascular disorder.
Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with pyramidal involvement; lasting distal muscle wasting and foot deformity are common manifestations, generally exceeding 30%.
Thymic epithelial origin has no anatomical axis in this scheme; thymoma is not lymphoma, and associated autoimmune diseases or immunodeficiency are separate conditions.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm is a vascular wall disorder; brain injury requires a hemorrhagic or ischemic complication and is not inherent.
Immune-mediated ulcerative inflammation involves the entire colon; extraintestinal associated diseases are not inherent to pancolitis.
Sarcoma originates in the paranasal sinus; sinuses belong to the pulmonary airway axis.
Congenital cardiac disease, skeletal abnormalities and developmental disability define this syndrome; strabismus 8/14 and ptosis 7/12 support ocular involvement.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with neuropathy; optic atrophy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each 3/8; lower-limb amyotrophy 30-79%. Elevated lactate alone adds no endocrine axis.
Familial neonatal epilepsy defined by neonatal seizures; no other organ damage is established.
